questions.stem: A call returns a 429 that carries no `retry-after` header, and its error code says the organisation reached its monthly spend ceiling. What does the module advise?

options.text: Back off with jitter, since capacity frees up within seconds
options.says: Ruled out because capacity failures are the ones where you "Wait for the header, or back off with jitter, then retry", and this response has no such header.

options.text: Hand it to a person, since only a higher limit or the reset restores access
options.says: The table sends "Your credential or account (401, 402, 403, a spend cap)" to a person, because "a spend cap lifts only at the monthly reset or with a higher limit", and "No retry can supply a key or a payment".

options.text: Split the work into smaller calls so that each one fits beneath the ceiling
options.says: Ruled out because the module's rule is to "retry only what can change by itself", and smaller calls do not change an organisation's ceiling.

options.text: Move the call to a fallback model, since this one is overloaded
options.says: Ruled out because a fallback model is the recovery for a refusal, where the table says "Use a fallback model, or reset the context", and this is not an overload.

questions.stem: After switching the model id, every call returns a 400 whose message says that a forced invocation is not supported for the model. The incident notes list four suspects. Which should the team investigate first?

options.text: The `tool_choice` field that the new release rejects
options.says: The migration table lists `tool_choice` of `any` or a named tool as returning a 400 on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, with the message "forced tool use is not supported for those models".

options.text: The prefilled turn that the new release rejects
options.says: Ruled out because the rejected prefill has its own message: "This model does not support assistant message prefill".

options.text: The thinking mode that the new release rejects
options.says: Ruled out because a rejected thinking mode is a "400, with a message that points to adaptive thinking and `output_config.effort`".

options.text: The capacity that the provider holds in that region
options.says: Ruled out because a 400 is a request status and capacity failures are "429 with `retry-after`, 529".

origin.section: Migration errors: your request, after a model change

questions.stem: A reply ends cleanly with stop reason `end_turn`, but the downstream code throws on it, and the logged output is a sentence followed by a fenced block of JSON. Which statement is true?

options.text: The fault is the integration's parser, so a test should script this sample
options.says: The table says an object between the first `{` and the last `}` makes it "The integration: the parser was too strict, so extract the object first", and the page says to prove a fix "with a test that scripts the trace".

options.text: The fault is the service's, so the call should be repeated until it is clean
options.says: Ruled out because the module's rule is to "retry only what can change by itself", and a repeat gives the same shape.

options.text: The fault is the model's, so the system prompt should forbid code fences
options.says: Ruled out because the trap warns "Assuming the model when the output is odd", and the output does hold the JSON.

options.text: The fault is the integration's limit, so `max_tokens` should be raised
options.says: Ruled out because a limit shows as a cut-off: "A reply that stops mid-sentence with status 200 is the integration's configuration", while this reply ends cleanly with `end_turn`.

origin.section: Integration or model: the question that decides

questions.stem: A bug in a tool-use loop is fixed in production on a Friday evening. Which follow-up does the module recommend?

options.text: Close the incident, since the fix was deployed
options.says: Ruled out because "A bug that is fixed without a test or an eval case will return", as the last trap puts it.

options.text: Add a note to the runbook and rely on the next on-call
options.says: Ruled out because a runbook note records the bug and does not test for it, and the page says "The bug cannot return unseen" once it is a case.

options.text: Scrub the trace and add it to the eval set as a case
options.says: The page says "A trace that went wrong in production is the best test case you will ever get: scrub it, give it an id and a tag, and add it to the eval set or the test suite."

options.text: Lower the retry budget so that the failure is less visible
options.says: Ruled out because a smaller budget hides failures, while the routine says to "note whether the application recovered".

origin.section: Fix at the right layer, then keep the case
